newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. jury deliberating Cuban banker's fraud case.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. jury deliberating Cuban banker's fraud case.

text.p: A jury began deliberating on Friday in the bank fraud case against a Cuban-born banker, his son and grandson, who are accused of defrauding Venezuelan depositors of millions of dollars.
The jury was sent home after five hours and was to resume on Tuesday in the case against Orlando Castro Llanes, Orlando Castro Castro and Castro Barredo.

They are accused of illegally using deposits in a family-controlled bank, Banco Progreso International de Puerto Rico (BPIPR), to prop up financial institutions they controlled in Central and South America.
Prosecutors say the three misled Venezuelan depositors to believe BPIPR was a safe off-shore bank, subject to tight regulatory control, and attracted deposits of more than $55 million.
The Puerto Rican bank closed in January 1995 with uninsured losses to depositors of more than $15 million. All three have been in jail since their arrests last April.

Castro, a Cuban exile accused of playing a key role in Venezuela's 1994 banking crisis, left Venezuela that year after arrest warrants were issued for him and several associates on charges of financial fraud and other crimes.
There were 44 witnesses during four months of testimony. Defence attorneys claim the charges are revenge by the Venezuelan government.

A key issue jurors face is whether New York has jurisdiction in the case. Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau has argued that millions of dollars in the alleged frauds were transferred through New York banks.
The defence claims no one in New York was defrauded.
Morgenthau has said he took on the case at the request of Venezuela's attorney general.

Meanwhile, Venezuelan Attorney General Jesus Petit Da Costa resigned on Friday. Da Costa told a news conference that some members of President Rafael Caldera's cabinet had hindered his efforts to extradite scores of bankers who fled justice during the collapse of the financial sector in 1994.
